claim: Indie hackers manually reconcile Stripe payments with spreadsheets monthly.
paraphrased_evidence: A founder described spending 4-6 hours each month exporting Stripe transaction CSVs and manually matching them against their internal records in Google Sheets. They complained about missing failed payment notifications and double-counting refunds.

claim: Multiple Stripe accounts create reconciliation pain for indie hackers.
paraphrased_evidence: A founder running two SaaS products under separate Stripe accounts described manually aggregating transaction data into a single spreadsheet to get a unified view of revenue. They said the process was error-prone and time-consuming.

claim: Syncing Stripe with CRM and email tools is a manual headache.
paraphrased_evidence: A founder explained they manually copy new customer emails from Stripe into ConvertKit and HubSpot every day because their Zapier integration kept breaking. They said it takes about 30 minutes daily and they've missed sending onboarding emails to new users.

claim: Indie hackers struggle with customer data sync between tools.
paraphrased_evidence: Another founder described using Make (formerly Integromat) to sync Stripe subscriptions to a Google Sheet, then manually importing that sheet into their email tool. They said the process fails silently and they often discover discrepancies days later.

claim: Manual invoicing is a recurring pain for indie hackers.
paraphrased_evidence: A B2B SaaS founder said they spend 2-3 hours every week creating custom invoices in Google Docs, converting to PDF, emailing clients, and then manually tracking payment status in a spreadsheet. They mentioned forgetting to follow up on overdue invoices multiple times.

claim: Following up on unpaid invoices is a manual chore.
paraphrased_evidence: Another founder described setting calendar reminders to check Stripe for unpaid invoices and then manually sending polite email reminders. They said it feels awkward and they've had clients pay weeks late because they forgot to follow up.

claim: Indie hackers manually monitor server uptime and logs.
paraphrased_evidence: A founder running a Node.js app on DigitalOcean said they manually check the server dashboard and error logs every morning. They had a 6-hour outage last month because they didn't notice a crashed process until a user emailed them.

claim: Indie hackers track SaaS subscriptions in spreadsheets.
paraphrased_evidence: A founder shared their Google Sheet for tracking 15+ SaaS tools they use, with columns for price, renewal date, and login URL. They said they discovered they were still paying for a tool they cancelled 3 months ago.

claim: Managing tool stack subscriptions is a manual overhead.
paraphrased_evidence: Another founder described spending an hour each month reviewing credit card statements to identify which SaaS tools they're still paying for and whether they still need them. They said they've accidentally paid for duplicate tools.

claim: Multi-channel customer support is manually managed by indie hackers.
paraphrased_evidence: A founder said they handle support via email, Twitter DMs, and in-app chat, and they track everything in a Trello board. They admitted to missing a support request on Twitter for 3 days because they forgot to check.

claim: Indie hackers manually manage affiliate programs with spreadsheets.
paraphrased_evidence: A founder running a referral program said they track affiliate sales in a Google Sheet, manually calculate 20% commissions each month, and send payments via PayPal individually. They said one affiliate complained about incorrect commission and they had to audit 6 months of data.
